identity.title: The dark side of the forces: assessing non-conservative force models for atomistic machine learning

problem.claim: The work investigates whether directly predicted, non-conservative interatomic forces are suitable for microscopic simulations.

gap.claim: Existing proposals suggest direct force prediction can improve accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and learn energy conservation, but its simulation applicability is questioned by the authors.

contributions.claim: Identifies and demonstrates fundamental problems associated with non-conservative force models, including ill-defined geometry-optimization convergence and instability in several molecular-dynamics settings.
Proposes combining direct force prediction with a conservative model to retain acceleration while reducing, rather than eliminating, backpropagation cost.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish energy conservation from rotational symmetry by arguing that conservation is difficult to learn, monitor, and correct in this context.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report ill-defined convergence during geometry optimization with non-conservative forces.
The authors report instability in various molecular-dynamics types when using non-conservative force models.
The authors report that energy conservation is harder to learn, monitor, and correct than rotational symmetry.

narrative_sequence.summary: Atomistic machine learning estimates energies and forces, where symmetry and conservation have traditionally been treated as essential.
Forces are usually obtained as derivatives of the potential energy to ensure energy conservation.
Recent work questions this constraint in favor of direct force prediction; the paper investigates its use in microscopic simulations.
The authors report optimization and dynamics pathologies and recommend pairing accelerated direct prediction with a conservative model.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the modeling choice directly to downstream behaviors—geometry-optimization convergence and molecular-dynamics stability—and separates rotational symmetry from energy conservation.

lessons.interpretation: A model-design claim is more informative when evaluated through the physical or algorithmic behaviors it affects, rather than only through prediction accuracy.
lessons.application: Frame a methods paper around concrete downstream failure modes and test each claimed physical property separately from symmetry-related properties.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method is intended only for static prediction and is never used in optimization or dynamical simulation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, model architectures, simulation conditions, quantitative results, or the exact conservative–non-conservative hybrid design.
The scope of “various types” of molecular dynamics and the precise meaning of ill-defined convergence are unspecified.
